items.headline: Gunnedah puts a draft AI policy on public exhibition, with guardrails on data and statutory decisions
items.summary: Gunnedah Shire Council has released a draft Artificial Intelligence Policy for public comment, setting out how staff, councillors, contractors, consultants, volunteers and service providers may use AI. The draft allows AI only where it offers a clear benefit over other options, bars personal or sensitive information from being entered into generative AI tools, prohibits AI from making statutory or legal decisions, and requires a person to review any AI-produced recommendation. It is on exhibition until 5pm on 13 August.
items.so_what: A smaller regional NSW council formalising AI rules is a sign the governance conversation is diffusing beyond the metro and peak-body leaders (MAV/ALGA's national working group, the Adelaide shared-AI partnership) to the rest of the sector. The draft's structure — a benefit test, a hard line against entering personal data into gen-AI, no AI statutory decisions, and mandatory human review — is a compact template any council still without an AI policy could adapt; awareness-only for now, worth watching for what the adopted version looks like after 13 August.
